question.problem:
The set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be ${a}_{2}$ if
${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14246751/assets/8d7ccb2401f2a03b484012d1c75cb4b9933297a228e634a172abbaec7c36a792.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
x_1 \mathbf{v}_1 + x_2 \mathbf{v}_2 = \mathbf{0}
$$

is $x_1 = x_2 = 0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14246751/assets/33c0a9aa1ed953fe67844af8bd0f566bcc51a14816b5d3d21438e5d5d2bfea7e.svg)
To see why, notice that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14246751/assets/a85b8c4eb41e1ba50b098a074c4ae29d88c131bed0fc82760d419eec04b26a15.svg)
In other words, the vectors $\mathbf a_1$ and $\mathbf a_2$ are parallel.

To see why this means that $\mathbf a_1$ and $\mathbf a_2$ are linearly dependent, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}-{a}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation

$$
x_1 \mathbf{a}_1  +x_2  \mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf{0}
$$

has the solution $x_1=\dfrac 1 3$ and $x_2=-1,$ which is different from $x_1=x_2=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.
